claims.text: Independent tensor checks and shifted-position control
claims.setup: On a single GB10, a serial reference run from embedding through all text layers and the trained iHC head, final norm and FP32 LM projection. Compare real prompt16 L0 and head plus independent fixed-input real L1/L2 CUDA oracles with locked bands; require exact embedding and discrete sets including unchanged L2 shared indices. Cycle the L0 score positions by one and require the identical comparator to reject the shifted logits. One fixed control set; categorical verdict, no sampling spread. Archive FP32 reference row shape [2048,120832] and complete.json artifact and source digests before scoring.
claims.command: eval/teacher.py control, then verify complete.json

claims.text: BF16 reduction-order null, all paired positions
claims.setup: Pinned Hy4 c10c0de5 and the frozen teacher-prompts.json listed in the reference SHA256SUMS, no chat wrapping, padding or generated tokens. Sixteen 1024-token prompts score every 16th position; each of four 4096-token prompts scores every 32nd through 2048, then 2048+floor(i*2048/192), i=1..192. Positions are one-based inputs whose logits predict the next token. Join by prompt ID and position; require identical token IDs, vocabulary order, row coverage and finite full logits. Replay four fixed 1024-token prompts (prose-01, code-01, prose-02, code-02) and all four 4096-token prompts from embedding to head on the same single GB10. Switch canonical microbatches 4 to 1 at 1024 and 1 to 2 at 4096. FP64 full-vocab KL(canonical || alternate); pair input positions. Compute token-pooled means across all 1280 pairs and separately across 512 unpruned and 768 pruned pairs. Resample whole prompts within length and genre, 1000 draws, seed 20261120; spread is percentile 95% CI. Report mean and its stratum-specific interval.
claims.command: eval/teacher.py teacher; verify null.json against complete.json

Pin weights, runtime, rank layout, cache dtype, slots, clock/power limits and argv; save clocks, watts, temperatures and per-node memory during every run. Pinned patched llama.cpp RPC with quiet even tensor split and verified per-link transport. Use exact UTF-8 and IDs from thinking-probes.json. Compare high against no_think and a render with only enable_thinking=False. Verify assistant prefix and greedy first token at positions 35/38; save ranks and probabilities for open/close tag, digit 4 and space on both builds when full logits are available. Replay twice per mode with fresh state, no draft, and capture actual reasoning trace on the short prompts. Record supported, contradicted or inconclusive against conditions fixed before the run. Spread is repeat agreement; exclude off from speed comparisons if mode is unverified.
claims.command: Run the speed measurements on the GGUF build and keep the client and engine logs

claims.text: Decode rate after a 4K prompt
claims.setup: Same four DGX Sparks over the direct cable ring, engines run sequentially, no other builds, downloads, suites or bulk copies. Pin weights, runtime, rank layout, cache dtype, slots, clock/power limits and argv; save clocks, watts, temperatures and per-node memory during every run. TensorFold TP=4 on stock NCCL IB; verify transport in each rank log. Use the frozen shared long-context manifest with exactly 4096 prompt IDs after templating, including BOS if used, and room beyond that depth for 48 generated tokens. C=1, greedy, plain and thinking off after mode verification, no cached prompt, loaded weights. Freeze one nonrepeating prose filler and three distinct ASCII key/value needles before either engine runs. Put the needle start at floor(0.10, 0.50 or 0.90 times prompt length) in separate prompts, with a final question requesting exactly the value on its first answer line. Verify positions and full prompt length in emitted IDs, pin the manifest hash and define unsupported context as unverified. Execute each placement once, with an untimed short warm-up and independent empty KV per request. Use 47 generated tokens after the first divided by elapsed monotonic time between the first and 48th. If exact token timestamps or the full budget are unavailable, leave the comparable metric unverified. Report the median of three timed repeats and the min to max range with width (max minus min). The three samples cover different needle placements; the reported width includes placement effects and is not the short-prompt A/A null.
claims.command: Run the long measurements on the full quant and keep the client and engine logs

claims.setup: Four DGX Sparks on the direct cable ring, TensorFold TP=4 over the direct RoCE relay for the per-layer sums (launch/ring.relay.env.example), no other jobs on the Sparks, weights already loaded. Full quant (default): routed experts EXL3 3.00 bpw, attention and shared experts EXL3 at the width in build.full.trunk (layers 75 and 76 shared-expert down_proj kept BF16), BF16 KV cache, FP32 output head. Token-by-token comparison of the first run's 128 greedy tokens with drafts on against drafts off on the same build, per prompt: prose thinking on, prose thinking off, code thinking on. Value per prompt: tokens that differ out of 128 and the first position where they differ. Every drafted token is the full model's own greedy pick, but verified in a wider batch, and BF16 rounds differently at another batch width; at a close call the pick can go the other way, and the text after it is a different continuation. Drafted output is therefore not expected to equal plain output. Drafted runs use the row-cost table measured on the same ring (TF_HY4_ROW_COST_TABLE from tools/row_cost_table.sh); the draft cutoff TF_HY4_DRAFT_MIN_MARGIN is off. Repeat option on (TF_HY4_REPEAT_STABLE=1, the kit default): the engine prices each draft depth from the row-cost table alone, with no wall clock, and the boot record says repeat_stable=on. With the option on a repeat gives the same tokens (speed.4k.repeatstable.same.exl3), so this comparison holds for every run. With it off the same comparison is quality.drafts.same.rsoff.exl3, and a later run of the same prompt can differ from that one.

claims.text: RigMark 1.3.0, one stream, decode rate, code workload, full quant
claims.setup: RigMark (https://github.com/alexellis/rigmark), a third-party benchmark, protocol 1.3.0 at revision 68800bf29cf1f85f834affdf81fe3e8703327342 with a clean tree, run as its standard suite (its DEFAULT SETTINGS): decode 5 runs per workload with an 8,192-token cap; prefill at 8,192, 32,768 and 65,536 tokens, 3 cold requests each with a fresh cache salt, each followed by an immediate replay; concurrency at 1, 2 and 4 streams, 3 rounds each, code workload, 256-token cap; temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 20260905. Every chat request carries reasoning_effort no_think (thinking off; with thinking on, a code reply ran to the 8,192-token cap before its answer: FINDINGS.md, finding 6). Four DGX Sparks on the direct cable ring at stock GPU clocks, TensorFold TP=4 over the direct RoCE relay for the per-layer sums (launch/ring.relay.env.example), no other jobs on the Sparks, weights already loaded. Full quant (default): routed experts EXL3 3.00 bpw, attention and shared experts EXL3 at the width in build.full.trunk (4b6b; layers 75 and 76 shared-expert down_proj kept BF16), BF16 KV cache, FP32 output head, 131,072-token window. Drafts on (DFly2 4-bit drafter, row-cost table measured on the same ring), repeat option on (TF_HY4_REPEAT_STABLE=1). The server runs one request at a time (SERVE_PARALLEL=1): concurrent requests wait in a first-in first-out queue, and there is no prefix cache across requests. Value: RigMark's single-stream median decode rate over the 5 runs of the code workload (decode.code.decode_tokens_per_second.median), streamed reasoning included. Spread: min to max over the runs, and the completion gate count.
